We wonder whether the results of this section are valid when restricting to fams with the uap. These are not in general. For example, let a ⊆ ω be the set of even numbers, B := P ( ω ), let B 0 be the field of sets over ω generated by a and let F ⊆ P ( ω ) be the filter of subsets of ω containing { 0 , 1 } . Let Ξ 0 be the (unique) probability measure on B such that Ξ( a ) = 2 3 (which is clearly uniformly supported). By Theorem 3.15, there is a unique probability fam Ξ on 〈 B 0 ∪ F 〉 extending Ξ 0 such that Ξ( b ) = 1 for all b ∈ F , in particular, Ξ( { 0 , 1 } ) = 1. Then, Ξ( { 0 } ) = Ξ( a ∩ { 0 , 1 } ) = Ξ 0 ( a ) = 2 3 and, naturally, Ξ( { 1 } ) = 1 3 . However, Ξ cannot have the uap because no singleton can have measure 2 3 under a probability fam with the uap (by Theorem 2.18). This also shows that Theorem 3.8 is not valid in general when restricting to the uap: both Ξ 0 and Ξ F are uniformly supported, but any common extension extends Ξ and thus cannot have the uap.

We can validate Theorem 3.15 to fams with the uap under further conditions.

Theorem 3.16. In Theorem 3.15, assume that B = P ( X ) and that B 0 contains all the finite subsets of X . If Ξ 0 has the uap, then so does Ξ . Likewise for 'uniformly supported'.

Proof. If all finite sets have Ξ 0 -measure zero, then the same is true for Ξ. So assume that Ξ 0 is uniformly supported with support P . Since B 0 contains all finite sets, all finite sets in P with positive measure must be singletons (by minimality). It is not hard to show that P is a support of Ξ, so Ξ is uniformly supported. □ 3 . 16

Similarly, we can validate the extension results when adding one set to the subalgebra.

Lemma 3.17. In the context of Lemma 3.11, assume that B = P ( X ) and that C contains all the singletons. Then, if Ξ has the uap, then Ξ ′ can be found with the uap. As a consequence, Ξ can be extended to a fam into K with the uap on the whole P ( X ) .

Here, 'uap' can be replaced by 'uniformly supported', even more, extensions of Ξ can be found with the same support.

Proof. The result is trivial when all singletons have Ξ-measure zero. So assume that Ξ is uniformly supported. The argument in the proof of Lemma 3.11, when replacing A by a support of Ξ, allows to find a uniformly supported Ξ ′ with the same support as Ξ. The rest follows by Zorn's Lemma. □ 3 . 17

We ask whether (iii) ⇒ (i) of Theorem 3.8 is valid when Ξ 0 and Ξ 1 have the uap for finding Ξ with the uap, under the condition that both B 0 and B 1 contain all singletons. If, say, Ξ 0 is free then Ξ 1 and Ξ must be free, but we do not know how to obtain an uniformly supported Ξ when Ξ 0 and Ξ 1 are uniformly supported.

Question 3.18. Assume that B 0 and B 1 are fields of sets over X , containing all the singletons, and Ξ 0 and Ξ 1 are uniformly supported fams with the uap on B 0 and B 1 , respectively. Assume that Ξ 0 and Ξ 1 are compatible (in the sense of Theorem 3.8 (iii) ). Is there a uniformly supported fam that extends both Ξ 0 and Ξ 1 ?

A strategy to solve this problem may suggest a short proof of Theorem 3.8.
